newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban not to pressure bin Laden to leave Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Taleban not to pressure bin Laden to leave Afghanistan.

text.p: Afghanistan's purist Islamic Taleban movement will not put pressure on wanted Saudi dissident Osama bin Laden to leave the country, a senior Taleban offical said on Wednesday.

Bin Laden, who was stripped of his Saudi Arabian passport in 1994, has been accused by a number of countries of having links with international terrorist groups and has his headquarters in Afghanistan.
"We will not put pressure on bin Laden to leave Afghanistan," Taleban Information Minister Amir Khan Mutaqi told journalists in Kabul.
Mutaqi said bin Laden was a guest, but that he would not be allowed to use Afghan soil to launch attacks on any other country.
"We are hospitable people, but we will not allow Afghanistan to be used to launch terrorist attacks," Mutaqi said.

The dissident, who called for a holy war against the United States last year, was "one of the most significant sponsors of Islamic extremist activities in the world today", the U.S. State Department said recently.
Mutaqi denied press reports that bin Laden had set up training camps near the eastern Afghan city of Jalalabad.
"The Taleban will never allow bin Laden to use Afghan territory for training camps or subversive acts against any other country," Mutaqi said.
Recent reports in the Pakistani press said a Pakistani delegation to the Taleban stronghold of Kandahar had expressed concern about bin Laden's presence in Afghanistan.
Bin Laden is reputed to have inhertited hundreds of millions of dollars from his father, a Saudi Arabian construction magnate.
The Americans and Saudi Arabians accuse him of using his fortune to finance attacks on American bases in Saudi Arabia.
Bin Laden has denied being involved.
The Taleban took the capital Kabul last September and now control more than three quarters of Afghanistan. They have vowed to implement strict Islamic Sharia law throughout the country.
